decision.location: Background, lines 28, 34, 46; Methods, line 68; Results, line 88; Discussion, lines 96, 120; References, lines 138-148
decision.quote: Abrazo was developed and tested in partnership with El Rio Community Health Center, a federally qualified health center in Tucson, Arizona; the initial program evaluation was carried out with breast cancer co-survivors. In Year 1, the first author (CM) and one trained promotora were co-facilitators of Abrazo and worked with 60 co-survivors. For Year 2, CM trained two promotoras who then delivered Abrazo. Year 2 served as a pilot test of Abrazo’s reproducibility, demonstrating it as an effective program that can be disseminated independent of the developer. In both years, results indicated statistically significant improvements for Abrazo participants in cancer knowledge and self-efficacy. This successful use of trained promotoras provided the basis for the dissemination initiative in Portland, Oregon.
decision.reason: The Portland replication study compares its pre-post Cancer Knowledge Questionnaire (CKQ) and self-efficacy outcomes against prior Tucson evaluation findings of Un Abrazo Para La Familia. Shipped row 735 (doi: 10.1002/pon.2108, published online 2011 / print 2013 in Psycho-Oncology, vol. 22, pp. 470-474, corresponding to target_index 0 in the coding file and the first reference in the source) already represents the initial Tucson evaluation report. Because the BioC source text strips all inline citation markers, and the body text refers to the prior Tucson work both as a two-year effort (Year 1 initial evaluation with 60 co-survivors and Year 2 pilot test of reproducibility, line 34) and in the singular as 'the Tucson sample' and 'both studies' (lines 46, 68, 88, 96, 120) while listing three Marshall et al. articles in the bibliography (Psycho-Oncology 2013 [online 2011], WORK 2013, and Journal of Cancer Education 2014), the supplied primary text does not establish whether Marshall et al. (2014) in Journal of Cancer Education is an alternate report of the same Tucson sample/evaluation already captured by shipped row 735, an earlier link in a replication chain, or the specific report whose item-level CKQ results are retested in Q2. Prior adjudication/state files do not exist for this work.

The Experiment 2 Results and Discussion explicitly state that 'Experiment 2 replicated the findings of Lu et al. This is a distinct original work and finding from shipped row 2399. Prior adjudication/state files do not exist for this work.
